name: Determining Whether One is a Teenager (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that receives a string that has the user name and age separated by a colon, and prints whether the user is a teenager. Make sure that the program handles all possible exceptions.

comments.content: We need to read and process the string that the user enters. To read the input string from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the name and age, separated by a colon.
We need to read the string that the user enters and store it in a variable. We read the string by calling the next() method.
This statement creates a JCheckAge1 object using the new keyword and empty parentheses. The variable jca holds a reference to a JCheckAge1 object.
This statement invokes the method checkAge of the jca and passes the string received from the user as its argument.

This method checks the string that is specified as the method's parameter and determines whether the user is a teenager. We define this method as public to provide access to this method from outside of the class. Also, we define its return type as void, as it does not return any value.
We need to split the given string into the name and age and store them in a string array.
We use split() method with ":" as its argument because we want the split method to separate strings using the colon character.
The try blocks tries to execute the code within it. The statements in the try block may throw several types of exception.
If an error is encountered, the try block code execution is stopped and transferred down to the catch block(s).
lst[0] gives us the element at index 0 of the array that represents the user name in the given string.
lst[1] gives us the element at index 1 of the array that represents the user age in the given string. We convert this value to an integer by using the Integer.parseInt() method.
Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents an integer.

To determine whether the user is a teenager, we need to check whether the user's age falls within the range from 13 to 19 (both inclusive). If it is, then we could conclude that the user is a teenager.
If the integer is in the range from 13 to 19 (both inclusive), then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement concatenates the name and the given text and prints the result of concatenation. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

Note that we concatenate the content of two strings using the + operator. Also, note that the concatenating and printing are done in the same line. That is, we don't have to store the concatenated string to a new variable at first and then print it in the next line.
If the above if test fails, we conclude that the user is not a teenager.

We need to handle the ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. This error occurs when the try block accesses the element at the index that does not exist in the array. This happens when the name and age are not separated by the colon. In that case, the array will have one value and an exception occurs when we try to access the element at index 1 of the array.
The body of this catch block gets executed only if the index 1 could not be found in the array. Otherwise, the body of this catch statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
We need to handle the NumberFormatException. This error occurs when the second value in the array is not an integer and we call the method Integer.ParseInt() to convert that value to an integer.
The body of this catch block gets executed only if the age in the given string is not an integer. Otherwise, the body of this catch statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the error that caused the NumberFormatException. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
